chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the people of the religions (non-Muslims), how are they made to take an oath? He said, 'Do not make them take an oath except by Allah.'

key_terms.يُسْتَحْلَفُونَ: Are made to take an oath

ai.seo_question: How should non-Muslims be made to take an oath in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential principle of *istihlaf* (administering oaths) for non-Muslims in Islamic courts, emphasizing the exclusivity of Allah’s name to avoid syncretism with their specific religious identities. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on maintaining theological purity in legal proceedings, ensuring that the oath invokes the universal Creator rather than sectarian deities or scriptures.
